ingredients.cook_qty: 1 1/2 tbsp for the batter plus 2 tbsp for dusting

instructions: At least 1 hour ahead: in a wide bowl, whisk 1 3/4 cups flour, 1 1/2 tsp yeast, 1 1/2 tbsp of the sugar and 1/2 tsp salt. Stir in a scant 1 cup (225 ml) of lukewarm water until the batter is smooth. Cover the bowl and leave it somewhere warm for 1 hour, until the batter has doubled and is bubbly.

Meanwhile, cut each hot dog in half and cut each string cheese stick in half. Push a piece of hot dog onto a wooden skewer, then push a piece of cheese on after it so they sit end to end. Make 8 skewers and keep them in the fridge until you're ready to fry.
Put the panko on a plate.

When the batter has risen, pour the oil into a deep, heavy pot, about 2 inches deep, and heat it over medium heat to 350°F (177°C). You're cooking at 350°F, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Drop in a spoonful of batter. It should bubble right away and float.
Dip a skewer into the batter and twist it until it's coated all over. Roll it in the panko and press the crumbs on, covering the cheese end completely.
Fry 1 or 2 skewers at a time for 3 to 4 minutes, turning them now and then, until they're deep golden. Transfer them to a rack to drain, and coat and fry the rest the same way.
While they're hot, dust each one with some of the remaining 2 tbsp sugar. Serve with ketchup and mustard drizzled over the top.
method_notes: Beyond Kimchee (4.94 from 30) leads: a yeast batter that rises for an hour, a sausage and mozzarella skewer, a panko crust and frying at 350°F. Aveline Cooks agrees on the yeast batter but adds an egg and potato on the outside; Real Mom Kitchen uses a baking powder batter with no rising. The lead's frozen fries and American cheese slices are optional there and left out here. Halved from the lead's batch of 8 sausages to make 8 skewers.
